Build a detection set

Source: R/detset.R
detset.Rd

A detection set holds the detections, the receiver deployments and, optionally, the animals, with the column names of the positionR table contract. It also holds the receiver listening days, an append-only processing log and metadata. Every later step in detqc takes one.

Usage

detset(detections, deployments, animals = NULL, crs = 4326, tz = "UTC")

Arguments

detections

A data frame with datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter and animal_id, as read_detections() returns.

deployments

A data frame with receiver_serial, station_id, deploy_datetime, recover_datetime, deploy_lat and deploy_lon, as read_deployments() returns.

animals

Optional data frame with one row per animal and transmitter and at least animal_id and transmitter, as read_animals() returns.

crs

EPSG code that the detset records for later steps, such as a projected code for coordinates in metres. The default, 4326, is geographic. deploy_lat and deploy_lon are always WGS 84 whatever this is.

tz

Time zone of any datetime column given as text. Text is read in this zone and converted to UTC. Datetime columns that are already POSIXct must be in UTC.

Value

An object of class detset: a list of detections, deployments, animals, listening, log and meta. meta$sources lists the files the import functions read, from the source attribute of each table, and the first log record counts the rows the import functions set aside. When the deployments carry download_datetime, the detections gain the logical column after_download: TRUE for a detection after its deployment's recorded download and before the deployment ends. The set keeps these detections; audit_listening() keeps their days "not_downloaded", and the check detections_after_download of check_detset() lists them. The column passes through the filters, so later steps can read it. Where the download time on the sheet is wrong, correct it and build the set again. The log record counts them.

Details

Each detection is matched to the deployment of its receiver whose interval holds it. The interval is half-open, deploy_datetime <= datetime < recover_datetime, so a detection at the moment of a receiver swap belongs to the later deployment. A deployment with no recover_datetime is open. The matched station_id replaces any station_id the detections carried. Detections that match no deployment keep their own station_id, or NA, and stay in the set: no row is removed here. A detection or deployment with no receiver_serial matches nothing.

Receivers are matched on receiver_serial as written. A detection that matches no deployment that way is matched again on the bare serial, so "VR2Tx-480013" finds the deployment of "480013" and the reverse; its receiver_serial then takes the deployment's form, which the listening days use too. Only a known receiver family (VR, HR, TBR and others) followed by three or more digits is read as model and serial. The log counts these matches, and detset() warns when fewer than half of the detections match a deployment.

A deployment sheet that records stations and no receiver serials, as OTN's deployment CSV does, is matched on station_id and time instead: a detection that matched no deployment by serial takes the serial-less deployment of its own station_id whose interval holds it. The log counts these matches.

A deployment that ends at the moment it starts can hold no detection under the half-open rule. It is dropped with a warning and counted in the log. A deployment that ends before it starts stops detset() when a detection is on its receiver (or at its station, for a deployment with no serial); the message names the row and points to check_detset(), which lists every such row. On a receiver no detection is on, as in the network-wide GLATOS receiver file, it is set aside with a warning and counted in the log.

Blank text, "" or spaces, in animal_id, transmitter, receiver_serial or station_id is a missing value: data.table::fread() reads an empty column as "", which would otherwise name an animal. The log counts the values read as NA.

When animals is given, a warning counts the detected transmitters it lists when that is none, or when they carry under 5% of the detections. animal_id is filled from it by transmitter for detections that have none; a detection whose own animal_id disagrees with the animals table keeps its own, with a warning that counts them. A transmitter listed on more than one animal, as after tag reuse, is filled by release time when every one of its animals has a distinct release_datetime: a detection goes to the animal released last at or before it, and a detection before the first release stays NA. Where a release time is missing or shared, the transmitter fills nothing. The log counts both kinds.

See also

validate_detset(), detset_log()

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
dets
#> <detset> 3,297 detections of 4 animals (4 transmitters), heard on 14 of 20
#>   receivers at 14 of 20 stations
#>   2024-06-02 to 2024-06-10 (UTC); 20 deployments; 4 animal rows; 220
#>     receiver-days deployed (listening not audited)
#>   log: 1 step (detset)
detset_log(dets)[, c("step", "fn", "rows_before", "rows_after", "removed")]
#>     step     fn rows_before rows_after removed
#> 1 detset detset        3297       3297       0
